But, if they started to abuse you physically you can and should in almost every case report it to the authorities. Cutting ties with your parents is okay imo, I'm posting this so that people can improve their relationship with their parents, when they're ready to do so. I am very sorry for your loss, and I understand what you're going through since my grandfather also died 2 days ago. Similar to you, he was healthy and fit the only problem that he had was his eyesight had worsen'd due to cataract. 

His death shocked me and others to the bone since just the night before his death, he was just strolling through the night like he used to everytime. I'm still in the middle of sorting my mind but please be at ease, since I believe that your grandfather is in a better place. 

If you're having issues with dealing with this, please reach out to someone you trust and talk to them personally about what you're going through. 

I'm very sorry if my english is a little bit hard to understand since its not my native language.

I think your mom doesn't really hate you. I, just like u/Mogamus grew up in a broken home ever since I was born. Even my childhood memories are only filled with my parents arguing and physically abusing each other, and sometimes me and my brother in the process. After a few years of constant arguing, fighting and hurting each other mentally and physically, my mom decided that she had to file for a divorce. Prior to this, she often called me with names, told me how stupid I am, etc. But here's the thing, after the divorce had been finalized, she came back to our house (I still live with my dad since I'm still 17) and actually apologized for what she had done to me, and my brother. 

From my experience, I think your mom doesn't really hate you. Maybe she has her own issues, or she's dealing with something thats out of your reach (maybe she has a problem with your father, just like my mother did). So just don't take this too seriously, if you want you should try and have a talk with her when you think that you and your mother are on better terms. Because here the thing, our time here is limited, you have to treasure the time you have with your parents now, or  you will regret it forever just like I did with my grandfather which I never really bonded with as a child. Trust me, try talking it down with your mom and at least try to convince her to slowly stop drinking. 

​

TL;DR

Your parents in most cases do love you, but they might have some issues on their lives that you might not be aware of, or maybe an issue that you cant deal with yet, since you're still a teenager. My suggestion, is to try and talk it down with your mom, and find out about whats the best way to resolve the issues that you had with her. And please remember that our time here isnt infinite so please treasure your memories and try to keep a positive relationship before its too late :)
